placements.why: The deployment gate decision is an architectural concern — it constrains how systems ship through mandatory preconditions. This strata category holds architectural decisions about system structure and deployment control.
placements.title: architectural decisions constraining system deployment and structure
placements.frame: What architectural and process decisions shape how systems are built, deployed, and controlled?

placements.title: deployment made conditional on signed manifests as a security gate
placements.frame: How is deployment control performed as a mandatory precondition rather than as a discretionary practice?
placements.why: All three segments contribute to the theme of deployment gates as settled security requirements: src-1 issues the directive mandating signed manifests, src-2 provides the motivating incident (unsigned artifacts reaching staging) as evidence for the gate, and src-3 ratifies the decision as structured record with scope and ownership.
